title: What Is UX Design? - An Introduction (Full Guide For 2024)

best.what: microwave/toaster/Norman-door examples of good vs bad UX, very teen-relatable

why: Clear, correct, relatable intro to what UX means (meet needs, easy to use, control, delight) with concrete non-digital examples; ~2 min at the end is a blooper reel, skip that.

title: What Does A UX Designer Actually Do? (In 2024)
why: Walks through real job ads (Tesla, Gorillas, Carhartt) to explain the UX role - useful for someone job-hunting, not for a kid building a project.

title: The UX Design Process For Beginners! (The 5 Key Stages)

best.what: the Uber example: how observing pain points (understand) drove their two biggest fixes

why: Clean, correct walkthrough of understand/analyze/ideate/validate/iterate with a real concrete example (Uber). Directly reusable framing for the course's planning/scoping unit.

title: How To Create Your First Wireframe (A UX Tutorial)

best.what: live hand-sketch of a login screen, then rebuilt in the free tool wireframe.cc

why: Exactly the low-fidelity planning-before-building skill kids need before they ask Gemini to build a screen; short, hands-on, and the tool is trivial/free so it transfers even though kids won't use it directly.

title: UX Design: 5 Essential Portfolio Tips! (For 2024)
why: Portfolio/job-hunting advice, off-topic for the course.

title: What UX Hiring Managers Actually Want To See!
why: Breaks down junior/mid/senior job ads (Deloitte, Adobe, Amazon) - pure hiring content.

title: The Essential UX Interview Questions (And How To Answer Them!)
why: Job-interview coaching, off-topic.

title: UX / UI Portfolios - 3 Essential Tips! (2023)
why: 1-minute portfolio tips, career content, too thin to be useful anyway.

title: What Is Inclusive Design - An In-depth Introduction (2021)

best.what: concrete before/after examples: Trello colorblind-mode patterns, gender-neutral toothbrush icons, abstract profile placeholders, Facebook's gender/pronoun fields

why: Substantive, well-argued intro to accessibility/inclusive design with real screenshots (WCAG, imagery, language, AI bias, voice UI bias); 41 min and touches identity/discrimination topics a facilitator should frame for young teens, but the content itself is accurate and directly useful.

title: UX / UI Design Portfolio Reviews (2022)
why: Hiring-manager critique of three job-seeker portfolios - career content.

title: UX / UI Design Portfolio Reviews + Feedback (2022)
why: Same format as the other portfolio-review video, duplicate of ePiz3jtLk-k - career content.

title: What Is Information Architecture? (UX Design Guide)

best.what: mental models, cognitive load and visual hierarchy demoed live on Amazon's real site (search, filters, category structure)

why: Directly teaches how to structure and organize information/screens before building - a core planning skill for kids designing an app's navigation and database. Great real-site walkthrough (Amazon, 1990s web vs Apple).

title: UX Research - Get Started With Qualitative User Research (2023)

best.what: step-by-step interview guide: research brief, screening, open vs leading/closed questions

why: Practical, low-budget, teen-doable guide to interviewing 5 people to find out what users actually want before building - maps directly onto 'describe and test' in the kids' workflow.

title: A Beginner's Guide To UX Writing (Full Guide)

best.what: what microcopy is and why it matters (Hawaii missile-alert error), the UX-writing process, and a critique of five real 404-page texts (Mailchimp, US/German Amazon, Berlin.de, Disneyland)

why: 60-min recorded webinar; the first ~33 min is a genuinely good, example-rich lesson on writing clear button/error/menu text (a real gap for vibe-coded apps). The back half is a live chat-reading writing exercise and Q&A that's messy to watch and needs a guide to pull out.

title: UX Design Trends 2022 (And The Future Of UX…)
why: Dated 2022 trend speculation (AR/VR, web3, the metaverse, remote work, personal branding) - outdated and not a teachable concept for the course.

title: Become a UX Designer in 2024 - A Step by Step Guide!
why: Career-change roadmap (bootcamp vs university, networking, portfolio) - off-topic for the course.

title: Notion (For UX / UI Designers) - A Full Guide (2023)
why: Tool tutorial for building a UX knowledge hub / job-application tracker in Notion - not part of the kids' stack (Apps Script + Sheets) and mostly career-prep framed.

title: A Day in the Life of a UX Designer (2023)
why: Vlog-style day-in-the-life of a working designer (standups, meetings, wireframing in Figma) - career/workplace content, not a taught concept.

title: Free UX Design Course For Beginners! (Start Today!)
why: A promotional walkthrough of CareerFoundry's own paid-funnel free short course (describes what's in each of its 6 emails) rather than teaching the content itself.

title: The Essential UX Design Trends to get ahead of in 2023
why: 2023 trend speculation (super-apps, generative AI, planet-centric design, tech layoffs); its one solid nugget (content design/UX writing) is covered far better and hands-on in hsMLqUFtPbU, so this is a dated duplicate.

title: How I'd Learn UX Design in 2024 (If I Had to Start Over)
why: Career-change advice (budget, learning style, portfolio, LinkedIn/networking) - entirely career-track content.

title: Using AI for UX Design is Incredible! - (An UX / AI Introduction: 2024)

best.what: AI pitfalls for design work: over-reliance, biased training data, lack of transparency, prompt quality, staying 'in the driver's seat'

why: Good AI-literacy material (how AI models work, where it helps vs. where it misleads) once you strip the specific tool demos (ChatGPT/Midjourney/Notion AI don't map onto the kids' Gemini-only workflow); best used by the teacher to frame a class discussion, not shown raw.

title: UX Job Seekers - Do This As Soon As You Can...
why: Networking and LinkedIn job-search tactics - career content.

title: Best UX Tools Unveiled!
why: 2-minute vox-pop of designers naming their favorite tools (Figma, Mural, pen and paper) - no teachable content, just opinions.

title: "Nobody Knows How AI Will Impact UX Design"
why: Vox-pop of designers giving hot takes on AI and job security - opinions, not a taught concept; duplicate in spirit of vyWFS4DPpqA which actually teaches something.

title: The UX Design Resource You Need!
why: Vox-pop of designers naming favorite resources (Nielsen Norman, Google, app-store reviews) - no real teaching content.

title: UX Design in 2023?
why: Vox-pop reassuring career-changers it's 'never too late' - pure career content.

title: Top UX Design Companies...
why: Vox-pop of designers naming favorite-UX companies (Spotify, Airbnb, Duolingo, Headspace, Google) with no explanation of why beyond taste - too thin to teach anything.

title: Quickest Ways to Become a UX Designer!
why: Vox-pop of quick career-advice soundbites - career content.

title: Product Design vs. UX Design - Which design role is right for you? (2024)
why: A job-title/role-boundary debate aimed at people choosing which job postings to apply to - off-topic for kids who won't be applying to either role.
